x: John Bicourt turned out to give us a 5000m/1500m double and Ian Duncan, fitting into our team very nicely, scored well in the 'B' 1500, but again the most exciting race was the 4 x 400 metres relay.

After two miles Bill Weller and Ian Duncan, with Colin Pearson in their slipstream, had broken clear of the field and as they took the dip past the "Crooked Billet" Laurie O'Hara was a full 20 metres astern.

Ian Duncan was also absent, competing successfully in a University race, while Jim Rimmer seemed to have more than a little difficulty keeping his shorts on and even with second-claimer John Abberton of Poly H in our colours Ranelagh had no difficulty in beating us to the line.

At last it appeared that Laurie's time might be drawing to a close as Ian Duncan, less than half the master's age, stuck to him like glue for two laps and even ventured to match strides side by side on occasion.

Ian Duncan undertook a daunting double by turning out in the 5000 metres and steeplechase yet still clocked a couple of good times. Our younger members made their presence felt on both field and the track with Matt King picking up 6 points in the heavy events, Mark Shippen beating all other competit…
After a fast start the front of the field soon split up, led by last year's rivals Ian Duncan and Laurie O'Hara - meeting for the first time this season.

Ian Duncan looked as though he might pull away early on but suffered a bad fall and did not make his move until the third lap. By this time he and O'Hara had opened up a clear lead over Rimmer and Williamson who had started too fast and struggled to hang on for the second half of the race.

Ian Duncan took over from Pat O'Connor as our leading runner; he was well up the field for the whole race and finished 13th. Simon Holmes was our second scorer for most of the race but was tiring at the end and O'Connor, timing his run to perfection, just got home in front.

Ian Duncan ran a steady race to win from second claim member John Stow with the evergreen Laurie O'Hara yet again dipping under 30 minutes. The handicap was jointly won by the improving Youth John Gladwin and by Steve White, with Junior Mark Sinclair showing very good form to gain 3rd place.
It was surprising, therefore, that Ian Duncan should chose this race the week before the Southern relay and disastrous that he should injure himself limping home in over 2 hours.
With Ian Duncan, John Bicourt and John Jackson all crying off in the preceding week Gordon Biscoe aged visibly as the day of the Southern 12 stage relay approached.
This time it was left to Ian Duncan, somewhat unfit having just completed his university studies, to drag our team round and at least keep it in the respectable half of the field teamwise.
Led home again by Ian Duncan showing welcome signs of a return to form, it is worth noting that our team on this occasion included some of our most regular performers this season.

With Ian Duncan and Alan McIntosh running in the Scottish Championships on the same day and with L. O'Hara, John Jackson, Lionel Mann, John Bicourt, Simon Holmes and Simon Williamson out of action for various reasons, it was left to the old team of Pat O'Connor and Jim Rimmer to lead the charge on our behalf.

Although we had Ian Duncan back in action it was virtually the same story, as reported elsewhere, for the Southern Championships. With the talent and strength some of the other clubs have these days we just cannot afford to be without our strongest teams on these occasions.

Ian Duncan who we thought might return to his native Scotland after his University studies is, thankfully, still with us, and in addition we have been pleased to welcome Alan McIntosh from north of the border.

It is ironic that fate should choose this race for people like Ian Duncan, Pat O'Connor and Bob Smith, some of the seasons most consistent and reliable performers, to have a bad one.

Ian Duncan continues his fight to regain fitness. Graham Macky although running very well declared himself dissatisfied with 35th position and we look forward to seeing what he calls a satisfactory performance.
Ian Duncan, now based in Scotland, and Stuart Paton both ran with distinction in the Scottish Championships just one week prior to the English equivalent at Parliament Hill.
Ian Duncan who has improved remarkably with every race this winter outkicked Graham Macky up Cambridge and maintained a clear lead to the finish.
John Bicourt and Paul Richley continued to keep hopes high but Ian Duncan failed to repeat his 5¾ form and continues to find this race his bete noir.

Included among these were Ernest Obeng (Exams), Snowy Brooks ('fm), Ian Duncan (injury), Stuart Paton (representing SCAAA), Mark Lindsey Bailey and Paul Whitby (both moved North), John Aska, Dave Bailey, Kevin Clarke and several others.
